title: Games
empty: No accounts yet. Add a Steam profile, a Dota 2 account or a WoW character.
confirmDelete: Delete {{name}}? Saved matches and achievements will be deleted too.

dota.steamIdHint: A number from OpenDota/Dotabuff or a steamcommunity.com/profiles/… link. “Expose Public Match Data” must be enabled in Dota.
dota.noMatches: No matches — match data may be hidden in Dota settings

hidden.title: Match history is hidden
hidden.text: OpenDota can’t see your matches. In Dota 2 open Settings → Options → Social, enable “Expose Public Match Data” and press refresh here. Downloading the history takes from a few minutes to a few hours.

dota.empty: No Dota 2 accounts yet. Add one — only a Steam ID is needed.

activity.title: Activity
activity.summary: {{matches}} matches on {{days}} days over the last year

dota.loadFailed: Could not load the Dota statistics. Reload the page; the saved matches are not lost.
dota.pendingResults: Steam has not told the result of {{count}} matches yet: they are filled in with every sync and are not counted in the win rate.

wow.realmHint: Realm slug as in the armory URL: “Howling Fjord” → howling-fjord
wow.credentialsHint: Create a client at develop.battle.net → API Access (any redirect URL, it is not used). Keys are stored encrypted on the server.
wow.empty: No characters yet. Save the Battle.net keys (Settings → Integrations) and add a character.

guide.1: Open develop.battle.net, sign in with the Battle.net account and go to API Access → Create Client.
guide.2: Any name; a Redirect URL is required — https://localhost will do; tick nothing else and create.
guide.3: Copy the Client ID and the Client Secret and paste them here, then add characters on the Games page.

errors.notFound: Account not found. For Dota, check that match data is public; for WoW, check region, realm and name.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. If you are adding WoW, save the Battle.net keys first.

widget.empty: Add accounts in the Games section

opendota.title: Dota 2 statistics
opendota.hint: Optional. Without a key OpenDota gives a small shared number of requests a day, and matches may come late. A key from opendota.com/api-keys lifts the limit; every Dota account takes a key of its own.
opendota.label: API key
opendota.noAccounts: Add a Dota 2 account on the Games page first.

guide.1: Open opendota.com and sign in with the Steam account.
guide.2: Open opendota.com/api-keys and create a key: the page tells what it costs.
guide.3: Paste the key next to the Dota account it is for; the account is refreshed with it at once.

steam.empty: No Steam accounts yet. Save the Steam key (Settings → Integrations) and add a profile.
steam.gamesHidden: Steam does not tell the library of this profile: open Steam → Profile → Edit Profile → Privacy Settings and make “Game details” public.
steam.profileHint: A link to the profile, its Steam ID64 or the custom name from steamcommunity.com/id/…
steam.keyHint: The key from steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey (any domain name will do). One key reads all your Steam accounts: the library with hours and achievements and the Dota 2 match history.

guide.1: Steam gives keys only to accounts that are not limited — ones that have spent about 5 USD in the store; free games do not count.
guide.2: Open steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey, type any domain name (for example localhost), agree and copy the key.
guide.3: Paste it here, then add your profiles on the Games page — one key reads all of them.
guide.4: For data to come: in the Steam profile make “Game details” public, in Dota 2 turn on “Expose Public Match Data”.
